summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11.4% to INR171.7 crores with 29.7% EBITDA margin, but H2 revenue fell to INR99.8 crores from INR115.9 crores.
summary.overview: Monarch reported audited FY26 consolidated revenue of INR171.7 crores (up 11.4%), EBITDA of INR51 crores (29.7% margin) and PAT of INR37.2 crores versus INR34.8 crores. H2 FY26 revenue was INR99.8 crores against INR115.9 crores in H2 FY25, with EBITDA of INR30.4 crores (30.5%) and PAT of INR24.3 crores. The order book stood at about INR615 crores at March 2026 and about INR740-750 crores after a INR130 crore Northern Railway win in FY27. Management announced a 100% acquisition of GMR Engineering Services in Australia for about AUD1.8 million, expected to close in early-to-mid July 2026, and a 16% dividend proposal.

segments.name: Roads and railways (DPR and infrastructure)
segments.commentary: Management said the order book is predominantly roads, railway DPRs and land acquisition; the INR130 crore Northern Railway order runs 36 months with 25-30% to be executed in FY27.

segments.name: Land acquisition
segments.commentary: Named as one of the main LOBs in the order book, alongside roads and railway DPRs; no separate revenue or order split disclosed.

segments.name: Geospatial
segments.commentary: Management said geospatial is a priority for coming years but the current order book has no material geospatial share; breakup not worked out.

segments.name: Overseas (GMR Engineering Services, Australia)
segments.commentary: Target to be 100% acquired for about AUD1.8 million; expected to add 8-10% of group turnover (about INR17-20 crores at management's framing), with EBITDA said to be near group level; 12 full-time employees and zero debt cited.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 revenue guidance; management said it expects to maintain past revenue, EBITDA and profitability growth, 'give or take some basis points'.
Order book of about INR740-750 crores (including INR130 crore Northern Railway order) is expected to convert over 1-3 years, paid on milestones.
Acquisition of GMR Engineering Services expected to close by first or second week of July 2026, subject to due diligence and FEMA approvals.
Unutilised IPO proceeds of INR66.43 crores planned to be spent in the coming year; machinery advance given in April 2026 after delays from geopolitical situation.
Somnath-Dwarka Expressway (about INR100 crores) awaiting alignment approval; 18-20 month execution once started; no revenue booked yet in FY26.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose from 630 (March 2025) to about 710-740 currently; management said it is recruiting, with ramp-up for a 140-person Settlement Commissioner project and Patna work for the INR130 crore order.
Company said it owns its drones, LiDAR, GEDO and digital twin equipment rather than renting it.
Office expansion: new offices in Ahmedabad and Nashik, joining Nagpur, Navi Mumbai, Delhi, Guwahati and Mumbai.
Capital work-in-progress includes a newly acquired office premises; intangible assets rose by INR1.07 crores, with digital twin spend not quantified.
Staffing lag of 2-3 months after tender award was cited as the main reason for execution slippage.
demand_pricing: Order inflows of over INR750 crores in FY27 year-to-date, including Northern Railway, Western Railway, Central Railway, North Central Railway, Nashik Municipal Corporation, Settlement Commission and Director of Land Records/MTDC.
Management said FY27 demand will be better than FY26 but declined to quantify; government share of order book is 3-4% or less, per management.
Named competitors: Aarvee (across LOBs), Genesys and Ceinsys (geospatial).
Government infrastructure capex of INR12.2 lakh crore for FY27 and railway outlay of INR2.93 lakh crore cited by management.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timeline for the INR615 crore order book and FY27 revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution is typically 1-3 years, with projects running 9 to 36 months; it declined to give FY27 revenue numbers, saying it expects to maintain growth in turnover and EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of other current assets and non-current investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed deposits of 3-12 months about INR80 crores (current); non-current FD INR13 crores; other non-current assets INR36 crores are mainly security deposits and EMD; total FD INR86.82 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 FY26 performance decline versus H2 FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to project billing and acceptance timing on the government portal; he argued FY26 full-year growth of 11.4% is the right benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: Expected economics of the Australian acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated revenue at 8-10% of group turnover on a gross-profit basis and said EBITDA will be near group level; exact figures to be reported in the next half-year call.

qa_highlights.question: Somnath-Dwarka Expressway project status?
qa_highlights.answer: Team and equipment are mobilised but work awaits government alignment approval; management admitted it is slightly behind timeline; no FY26 revenue booked.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and operating cash flow deterioration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables rose on volume and billing timing at year-end; aging is 100-105 days, INR7.5-8 crores over one year, and collections of INR55 crores pending are being pursued in April-May.

risks_watch: Revenue decline in H2 FY26 (INR99.8 crores vs INR115.9 crores) versus order book growth; conversion pace of INR740-750 crores order book is unclear.

Receivables and unbilled revenue: gross receivables about INR55 crores at March 2026 (up from about INR10 crores in FY24 per analyst); about INR7.5-8 crores is over one year; operating cash flow negative in FY26 per analyst.
Headcount growth of about 70% since March 2024 (417 to 710+) versus revenue growth of about 21% over two years per analyst; utilisation and staffing lag flagged.
Delays from government side on Somnath-Dwarka Expressway alignment and other projects; management says no penalties booked.
Australian acquisition closing in July 2026 subject to FEMA and due diligence; limited disclosure on valuation and target financials; IPO proceeds deployment (INR66.43 crores unutilised) timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the order book and long-term growth, but evasive on FY27 revenue, margins and utilisation, repeatedly declining to quantify. Management was defensive when questioned on H2 decline, receivables, cash flow and the Australian acquisition rationale.

So, as if like the commitment on a percentage is difficult to say at this moment of time because there may be certain projects which had a timeline earlier maybe preponed for two-three months or postponed because of some decisions from the government side.
